messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to improve the overdispersion poisson model in Stan
parts:
First let me repeat the model here:

data {
int J;
int y[J,22];
}
parameters {
vector[J] a;
vector<upper=0>[22] b;
vector<lower=0,upper=1>[22] w_ad;
real<lower=0> sigma_a;
real a0;
real b0;
real<lower=0> sigma_b;
}
model {
w_ad~uniform(0,1);
for(i in 1:J)
for(j in 1:22)
y[i,j]~ neg_binomial(exp(a[i])*exp(b[j])/(1/w_ad[j]-1), 1/(1/w_ad[j]-1));
a~normal(a0,sigma_a);
b~normal(b0,sigma_b);
}

From your writeup, the constraint on b should be <lower=0,upper=b>
if you want b in (0,1).

And I don't see where the -1 is coming from in (1 / w_ad[j] - 1).

For computing, you want to avoid repeated computations in loops.
It'd help if you use the same parameterizations in the writeup as
in the model if they're different and that's why there's a -1.

Shouldn't the loop on i be (for i in 1:I)? If not, you should probably
rename the variables to match, because it's confusing with an i and a j
and the i going from 1:J.

The loop would be better the other way around:

for (j in 1:22)
real wm1_inv;
real exp_b_j;
real wm1_inv_times_exp_b_j;
wm1 <- 1 / ((1 / w_ad[j]) - 1);
exp_b_j <- exp(b[j]);
prod <- wm1_inv * exp_b_j;
for (i in 1:I)
y[i,j] ~ neg_binomial(exp(a[i]) * prod, wm1_inv);

Then it'd be better if y were stored in transposed order, then you
could vectorize the inner loop to:

y[j] ~ neg_binomial(exp(a) * prod, wm1_inv);

If you want to come around next week to Daniel's and my office
some afternoon (927 SSW -- the floor below Andrew's office), we
can talk about the whole model in more detail because I don't
understand the constraints.

I'd say to read the negative binomial doc in the manual, but
I can't make sense of the second one --- there seems to be
a free-floating variable eta that should be defined as log(mu),
not free.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to improve the overdispersion poisson model in Stan
parts:
There's probably all sorts of reparameterization to play with here.
It's the negative binomial! We have two parameterizations built into
Stan and then you can start playing with exactly how overdispersion gets
estimated and related to the mean.

- Bob
